discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `d23386884`. The `afterRun` hook now awaits `next.afterRun(...)`, which resolves once the rule-based set is served. A one-shot run's `runtime.stop` therefore can no longer call `next.dispose` before the offer and debug-log entry are written, and the source, git and backlog read budgets bound the wait. The planner call and the connector refresh stay detached, and `plugin.test.ts` covers this by disposing right after `agent.run` while both are still pending.

Fixed in `d23386884`. `pruneSessionStates` still screens files with the async `stat`. For an expired file it now re-checks with `statSync` and removes it with `rmSync` with no await in between, so a state file rewritten while the first stat was pending is kept, as `session-state.test.ts` covers. A write from another process that lands between those two calls can still be lost, because there is no unlink-if-unchanged.

Fixed in `d11e7aca0`. `pruneSessionStates` now removes an expired file through `removeIfUnchanged`: it renames the file aside (atomic, so no write can interleave) and deletes it only if it is still the version whose age was checked (same inode, mtime and size); a version written since goes back with `linkSync`, which fails rather than overwrite a write that landed after the rename. `session-state.test.ts` covers a write after the last check and one that lands while a newer version is held aside.

Fixed in 631e30f11c by refusing the old set. Every state the plugin publishes now gets its own revision, including the refill after Skip and after Undo skip, since Undo skip had the same race. In your sequence, the `more` for Wrap up still carries the set the first Skip replaced, so it comes back stale: Next step stays, Wrap up stays visible, and the tray shows its stale note. Skip itself accepts a row from any set this turn, as Undo skip already did. The item id names the row's kind, so two quick Skips on named rows both land. A new test covers this sequence.

Fixed in f83618bd27. `begin()` now only stages the new epoch. `activate()` promotes it once the replacement session is resident. Until then the resident session keeps its slot state, viewers and UI chain, and keeps serving invokes. A start that fails releases only its staged epoch, so a failed reopen leaves the working chat's suggestions as they were. `clearPlugin` also takes the epoch now, so a plugin that fails while the replacement is starting can't clear the resident copy.

Covered by "serves the resident session while a same-id start is pending and after it fails" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, plus the staging cases in `store.test.ts` and `service.teardown.test.ts`.

Valid, and the window is wider than the comment says: `updateSessionStatus` in the persistence service retries a write whose status lock went stale, so when the two writes overlap the in-flight `running` fails its first attempt, re-reads the row and writes `running` on top of `cancelled`. The late writer always wins.

Fixed in "serialize session status writes so teardown's status lands last": status writes are chained per session on the same promise queue the compaction state already uses, so teardown's write waits for the in-flight one, and the shutting-down guard now runs when a write actually starts rather than when it is requested. The "drained prompt whose turn was still preparing" test now keeps the `running` write held across `stopSession` and asserts `cancelled` is not issued until it is released.

Valid, and it contradicts the comment a few lines above ("Once spawned, keep the shared startup lock until discovery is published. Cancelling a waiter must not let another waiter launch a duplicate daemon"). At `815be409c` the post-spawn probes had no signal; now both `probeHubForStartup` calls in the loop receive `signal`, so an abort throws an `AbortError` that the `catch` does not swallow, and the lock is released while the daemon is still booting. Impact is bounded by the OS-level `HubInstanceLock` (a duplicate daemon loses the singleton race), so low severity, but the fix is just dropping `signal` from those two calls; `deadline` already bounds them.

Implemented in `84db143`.

The response is claimed before the first asynchronous delivery step, so a second submission cannot resolve the same question. It is routed through the normal follow-up path while the claimed response continues delivering its attachments. I kept the session identity check and retained a per-attempt validity token so cancellation, replacement questions, delivery failures, and retries remain safe: an old callback cannot become current again after a retry, and a failed attempt releases only its own claim.

The focused VS Code suites cover the overlap, cancellation, failure/retry, and stale-callback cases and pass; SDK typecheck also passes. The separate display fix keeps the original pending-question text in the submitted event while preserving the expanded model prompt.

Implemented in commit `84db143`.

The pending ask response is now claimed synchronously before attachment preparation begins. While that claim is in flight, another submission cannot resolve the same `ask_question`; it falls through to the normal follow-up path instead. The claim is tied to the individual delivery attempt, so cancellation or replacement of the question invalidates older callbacks, while a delivery error releases only its own claim and leaves the original response retryable.

I added regressions covering overlapping text and attachment submissions, cancellation during delivery, delivery failure followed by a retry, and stale `isCurrent` callbacks after a replacement question. The focused VS Code suites pass (231 tests total), and the SDK typecheck passes.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
🟡 **bug** (medium)

Dropping `await this.checkpointTracker.commit()` means `saveCheckpoint()` can return before `lastCheckpointHash` has been written to the last `checkpoint_created` message. Your own NOTE states the attempt-completion flow needs that hash to be present: `ToolExecutor` calls `saveCheckpoint(true)` and is always followed by `addNewChangesFlagToLastCompletionResultMessage()` → `doesLatestTaskCompletionHaveNewChanges()`, which reads the latest checkpoint hash to decide whether to show the 'see new changes' button. With the commit now running in the background (and taking seconds on large repos), the hash is very likely still missing at that point, so the flag/button may silently stop appearing after `attempt_completion`.

**建议**: Keep a handle to the commit promise and await it when the caller needs the hash before continuing, e.g. capture `const commitPromise = this.checkpointTracker.commit().then(...)` and then `if (isAttemptCompletionMessage) { await commitPromise }` so the existing `saveCheckpoint(true)` contract is preserved while normal checkpoints stay non-blocking. If this is already handled elsewhere, a short comment stating where would help.

**证据**: `await this.say("checkpoint_created")`

Good catch, fixed in 98d674cfa. shutdownSession now deletes the slot only when it still points at the runtime being shut down, the same guard releaseSessionRuntime already had. Regression test: a stop stalled in the resident's agent shutdown while a same-id start registers the replacement; the replacement stays reachable afterwards (fails with session_not_found without the guard).

`request()` coalesces a newer request into `pending`, but it doesn't invalidate an already-active rebuild for the same reason — `cancellationGeneration` only moves in `cancel()` (line 40). So the active run's `isCurrent()` stays `true`, and once it finishes the newer request rebuilds the session again.

There's a correctness window here, not just redundant work. If the active rebuild has already snapshotted its config when the newer setting arrives, it installs the superseded one; and for checkpoint rebuilds it can replay a deferred follow-up from the shared `checkpointTransition` before the newer rebuild applies the latest setting — so a real message can run under the old checkpoint config.

I don't think bumping the generation here is a self-contained fix: the transition object is shared between the active and queued requests, and an invalidated rebuild returning from `replaceActiveSession()` can still clear `this.checkpointTransition` and stop the replacement. Either make a same-reason request explicitly supersede the active run with the transition ownership handled to match, or rename `isCurrent()` so it's clear it only means "not cancelled". A scheduler test for requesting a reason while that reason is actively rebuilding would pin whichever contract you pick.

Thanks — you were right on both counts, and the second one hid a real defect.

`isCurrent()` in a78223a means exactly "no newer request for the same reason has arrived": `request()` stamps a per-reason generation, and a running rebuild's context reads it live. `cancel()` and the per-reason cancellation generation are gone; nothing could reach them because `runTaskTransition` waits for the drain first.

The shared `checkpointTransition` is gone too. Holding a follow-up outside Core's queue meant nothing rendered it: a message typed during a turn after toggling Checkpoints vanished from the chat until the turn ended (this is what the e2e was failing on across all three CI platforms). Follow-ups now always go to Core's queue. The scheduler treats a session with queued prompts as busy, since Core drains the queue the instant a turn ends, and a send that settles after Core already started the next queued turn no longer flips the session idle. There is a scheduler test for a same-reason request during an active rebuild, and coordinator tests for supersession before replacement.

Valid catch — a cancel landing while a retry's `doStream()` was pending saw no active reader, and the freshly resolved stream was then drained unattended. Fixed by checking for cancellation at the top of each attempt and cancelling the fresh provider stream instead of attaching a reader; this also covers a cancel arriving before the pump's first read. Added a regression test ("cancels a retry attempt whose doStream() resolves after the consumer cancelled") that fails against the previous revision.

[P2] Clean up inherited pipes when the fallback settles. Resolving leaves stdout/stderr and their data listeners active. Reproduced: the hook returned after 1.02s, but Node stayed alive until its background child exited at 3.54s. A persistent child can keep the host alive and keep accumulating output. Add once-only pipe/listener and timer cleanup, with a test that checks host exit after settlement.

good catch, thanks!

The fallback now drops stdin/stdout/stderr (listeners included) right after it settles so the grandchild can't keep the host alive or keep filling the buffers. 

Added a test that counts the process's active pipe handles before and after — it fails on the old code (pipes stay until the grandchild exits) and passes now. Also, added a line to the hooks readme telling authors to give a backgrounded child its own stdio, since anything it writes to the inherited pipes after the hook exits is gone.
